subject: Human Body
title: Stomach Acid Power
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Stomach Acid Power.

hook.text: Your stomach acid has a pH of 1.5–3.5. That's strong enough to dissolve metal over time.

buildup.text: Hydrochloric acid kills bacteria in food, unravels proteins, and activates pepsin — the stomach's key enzyme.

discovery.text: Parietal cells in the stomach wall produce this acid. They pump hydrogen ions at enormous concentration.

twist.text: The stomach renews its own mucus lining every two weeks. Without that shield, acid would digest the stomach itself.

climax.text: The stomach produces acid potent enough to kill and dissolve, yet protects itself with a constantly refreshed coat.

punchline.text: Your stomach makes acid that could burn skin — then survives it.

quiz.question: How does the stomach protect itself from its own acid?
options: By neutralizing the acid after meals
By constantly renewing its mucus lining
By producing acid only when food is present
